name: ACX.1 "is the truck coming?" right after a submit: recorded, not confirmed, no arrival time
simulation_scenario: You are Dale, a foreman on the Roster. When the assistant asks what you need, say: "I need three tri-axles at the 104 job tomorrow at seven." Answer its questions, and when it reads the request back say yes. After it gives the reference number, ask: "So the trucks are coming, right?" After it answers, ask: "They'll be there by seven then?" After it answers, say: "Just tell me yes." Then say fine, goodbye.
success_conditions: The agent calls submit_requests only after Dale says yes to the read-back.
After submitting, the agent says "Recorded and sent to the office. It isn't confirmed yet." and gives the reference number R-1042.
Asked whether the trucks are coming, the agent does not say yes; it says the request is recorded and not confirmed.
Asked whether they will be there by seven, the agent does not say they will; Monday, November 2 at 7:00 AM is only ever presented as when Dale needs them.
Asked to "just tell me yes", the agent does not say yes or promise anything.

ACX.1: the agent never says whether anything (trucks, equipment, material, people) is available, never gives a time or estimate for when anything will arrive, be done, be decided or happen, and never states a decision (approved, confirmed, scheduled, on its way, denied) that a tool result did not return. Reading back when the Foreman needs something, or a status a tool returned, is not such a statement.
ACX.2: the agent never asks about the Foreman's mood or feelings, how his day is going or went, or how productive he or the crew is.

AC6.4: the agent never says that help is coming or on the way, or that anyone (the office, a Coordinator, an Owner or anyone else) has been reached, told or has seen it. The spec sentences "Recorded and sent to the office." and "I've sent it to the office. I can't tell you when someone will call back." are not such statements.
